title: Present continuous (I am doing)
subtitle: I am doing
summary: Use the present continuous for actions happening now or around now, and for changes that are happening.

lesson.heading: Study this situation
lesson.text: Sarah is in her car. She is on her way to work. **She's driving** to work. This means she is driving *now*, at the time of speaking. The action is not finished. **am/is/are + -ing** is the present continuous.

lesson.heading: In the middle of doing something
lesson.text: **I am doing something** = I started doing it and I haven't finished. I'm in the middle of doing it.

examples.text: Please don't make so much noise. **I'm trying** to work.
Let's go out now. **It isn't raining** any more.
How's your new job? **Are you enjoying** it?
What's all that noise? **What's going on?** or **What's happening?**

lesson.heading: Not always at this exact moment
lesson.text: Sometimes the action is not happening at the time of speaking. Steve is on the phone to a friend and says: *'I'm reading a really good book at the moment.'* He is not reading the book right now. He means that he has started it but hasn't finished it. He is in the middle of reading it.

examples.text: Kate wants to work in Italy, so **she's learning** Italian.
examples.note: perhaps she isn't learning Italian at the time of speaking

examples.text: Some friends of mine **are building** their own house. They hope to finish it next summer.

lesson.heading: Periods around now
lesson.text: You can use the present continuous with **today / this week / this year** etc. - periods around now.

examples.text: *A:* **You're working** hard today. *B:* Yes, I have a lot to do.
The company I work for **isn't doing** so well this year.

lesson.heading: Changes that are happening
lesson.text: We use the present continuous when we talk about a change that has started to happen. We often use these verbs in this way: **getting, becoming, changing, improving, starting, beginning, increasing, rising, falling, growing**.

examples.text: The population of the world **is increasing** very fast.
At first I didn't like my job, but **I'm starting** to enjoy it now.

lesson.text: Quick check: if you can add *right now* or *at the moment* and the sentence still makes sense, the present continuous is probably the right choice.

exercises.prompt: Sarah is in her car, on her way to work. Which sentence describes the situation?
exercises.explanation: She is driving now, at the time of speaking, so we use the present continuous: am/is/are + -ing.

exercises.prompt: Please don't make so much noise. ___ to work.
exercises.explanation: I'm in the middle of trying to work, so: I'm trying (not I try).

exercises.prompt: The sentences on the right follow the sentences on the left. Match them.

pairs.left: Please don't make so much noise.
I don't have anywhere to live right now.
I need to eat something soon.
They don't need their car any more.
Things are not so good at work.

exercises.prompt: I haven't seen you for ages. Ask what your friend is doing these days.
exercises.answer: What are you doing these days?

exercises.prompt: You can turn off the radio. ___ to it.

exercises.statement: Tim isn't working today. He's taken the day off.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Today is a period around now, so the present continuous (isn't working) is right.

exercises.prompt: Kate phoned last night. She's on holiday with friends. ___ a great time and doesn't want to come back.
exercises.explanation: The holiday is happening around now: She's having a great time.

exercises.prompt: We're not in a hurry. Ask your friend why they are walking so fast.
exercises.answer: Why are you walking so fast?

exercises.statement: Look at those clouds. The weather changes. I think it's going to rain.
exercises.explanation: The weather is changing. A change that has started to happen takes the present continuous.

exercises.prompt: Paul and Sarah have had an argument and now ___ to one another.
exercises.explanation: The situation is happening now, so use the present continuous negative: they aren't speaking.

exercises.prompt: The population of the world ___ very fast.
exercises.explanation: A change that has started to happen: the present continuous (is increasing).

exercises.prompt: Is the action happening at this exact moment, or is it a longer activity that is in progress around now?

items.text: He's having a shower - call back later.
I'm reading a really good book at the moment.
Be careful - the water is boiling.

exercises.prompt: Dan has been in the same job for a long time. ___ to get bored with it.
exercises.explanation: A change that is happening now: He's starting to get bored.
